slides.title: Title — Layout Gallery
slides.heading: Layout Gallery
slides.byline: Every slide names its layout — copy the ones you want
slides.notes:
layout: "title"

Fields: eyebrow, heading, subheading, byline.

Read this deck beside decks/gallery.json — each slide is a working example of its own JSON.

slides.title: title-content
slides.heading: title-content
slides.body: A heading with body text, bullets, or both. Text fields accept HTML, so emphasis works.
bullets: A plain string becomes a bullet

bullets.text: An object adds a second line
bullets.sub: Useful for a source, a caveat, or a short aside

slides.notes:
layout: "title-content"

Fields: eyebrow, heading, subheading, body, bullets.

Bullets take either a string or {text, sub}.

slides.title: section
slides.heading: section
slides.subheading: A divider between parts of a talk.
slides.notes:
layout: "section"

Draws a rule under the heading. Add "cls": "center" to centre it, as here.

slides.title: title-only
slides.heading: title-only
slides.notes:
layout: "title-only"

Just the heading. Use it when you want the room looking at you rather than the screen — the most underrated layout here.

slides.title: two-content
slides.heading: two-content

left.body: Two independent regions. Either can hold text…

slides.notes:
layout: "two-content"

left and right each take text fields, an image, or a media embed. Here the right side is an image.

slides.title: comparison
slides.heading: comparison

left.body: Each side gets its own subheading above the content.

right.body: Good for before/after, or two options you want weighed.

slides.notes:
layout: "comparison"

Like two-content, plus a subheading on each side.

slides.title: picture-caption
slides.heading: picture-caption
slides.body: A centred picture with its caption underneath, at a smaller size.

slides.title: content-caption
slides.heading: content-caption
slides.caption: A large media region beside a narrower column of explanation. Good when the picture needs a paragraph, not a line.
slides.notes:
layout: "content-caption"

The caption field fills the text column; image or media fills the wide region.

slides.title: media-right
slides.heading: media-right
slides.body: Text on the left, media on the right. The workhorse for most talks.
slides.notes:
layout: "media-right"

Takes all the text fields plus an image or media.

slides.title: media-left
slides.heading: media-left
slides.body: The same layout, mirrored. Alternate them so a run of split slides doesn't feel mechanical.

slides.title: media-caption
slides.heading: media-caption

image.caption: The caption sits under the frame, at a smaller size.

slides.notes:
layout: "media-caption"

A centred image or embed at moderate size. The caption lives on the image object, not the slide.

slides.title: media-full
slides.heading: media-full
slides.body: Text sits in a gradient panel along the bottom, so it stays readable over any image. Leave the text out for a picture with nothing on it.
slides.notes:
layout: "media-full"

Image or embed fills the slide. eyebrow, heading and body are all optional.

slides.title: grid
slides.heading: grid
slides.notes:
layout: "grid"

Two to four images with optional captions. Four lay out as a 2×2 rather than a row.

slides.title: Embed — local activity
slides.heading: An embedded activity
slides.notes:
A local HTML file, read at build time and inlined as the iframe's srcdoc. It travels inside the deck and needs no network.

"media": {"file": "media/activities/sorter.html"}

With no aspect, an activity fills whatever space the slide has and refits when the window, text size, or notes panel changes. Give it "aspect": "16:9" to pin a shape instead.

Sandboxed to allow-scripts. While you're clicking in it, arrow keys go to the activity — advance from your phone.

slides.title: Embed — external
slides.heading: An external embed
slides.body: If it can't load within six seconds, a QR code appears instead of a blank frame. Press R to retry.
slides.notes:
External embed. "media": {"src": "https://www.youtube.com/embed/…"}

Use the /embed/ URL form, not watch?v=.

pixi run build lists every slide like this one.

slides.title: cls: ask
slides.heading: cls: "ask"
slides.body: Any layout can be inverted to the dark treatment. Use it for questions and discussion stops.

bullets.sub: Slightly warmer paper — an aside or anecdote
Centres the content; combines with the others

slides.notes:
cls is independent of layout — combine freely, e.g. "cls": "ask center".

The remote flags ask slides so you can see a discussion stop coming.

slides.title: quad-chart
slides.heading: quad-chart
slides.subheading: Each quadrant gets a subtitle and either text or media.

quads.body: Summarise the constraint or tension in one short paragraph.

bullets: Run a pilot in one region

quads.body: Use the fourth box for the call to action, the next step, or the decision.

slides.notes:
layout: "quad-chart"

Use quads with exactly four entries. Each quadrant takes a subheading, plus body, bullets, an image, or media.

slides.title: blank (freeform)
slides.html:
Escape hatch

blank

A slide with no layout renders its raw html exactly as written. Full control when a layout doesn't fit.

Reach for this last — the layouts stay consistent, freeform slides drift.General advice
slides.notes:
layout: "blank" (or omit layout entirely)

Your markup goes in html and is used verbatim. The deck's own classes are available: eyebrow, lead, byline, dialogue, plus h1–h3, blockquote, cite, ul.

slides.title: End
slides.heading: Copy what you need
slides.body: Every slide here is a working example in decks/gallery.json.
